name: Typhoon
tagline: Free 1990s C database library in the style of Raima db_VISTA, but relational; long abandoned.
description: Typhoon is a C library for record-oriented databases on UNIX and OS/2, released by Danish developer Thomas B. Pedersen in 1994. Inspired by Raima's db_VISTA but relational rather than network-based, it lets you describe tables like C structs in a DDL file with primary, alternate and foreign keys, compile it with the ddlp tool, and then read and write records through C calls. It supported nested structures, unions, variable-length fields and referential integrity, but shipped without locking or transactions. Kaz Kylheku took over maintenance in 1999 with 1.11.x cleanup releases; a GitHub mirror exists, but there has been no development for decades.
statusNote: Unmaintained since Kaz Kylheku's 1.11.x releases (1999); only a 2018 GitHub mirror remains. Use SQLite, LMDB or Raima for embedded C storage.
developer: Thomas B. Pedersen; later Kaz Kylheku
strengths: Schema defined as C structures, compiled ahead of time for fast record access
Primary, alternate and foreign keys with referential integrity in a tiny library
Permissive licence and small, readable C source
weaknesses: No locking, logging or transactions in released versions
K&R-era C code, unmaintained for decades
useCases: Maintaining old C applications that use it
